questions.stem_latex:
$A$ and $B$ are two arithmetic series, where all the terms are positive.

In series $A$, the first term is $a$ and common difference is $d$. In series $B$, the first term is $M$ and the common difference is $D$.

Let $P=$ the sum of the first $n$ terms of $A$ and let $Q=$ the sum of the first $n$ terms of $B$.

parts.label: a
parts.latex: Show $\dfrac{P}{Q}=\dfrac{a+\left(\dfrac{n-1}{2}\right)d}{M+\left(\dfrac{n-1}{2}\right)D}$.

parts.label: b
parts.latex: Express $\dfrac{10^{\text{th}}\text{ term of A}}{10^{\text{th}}\text{ term of B}}$ in terms of $a,\ d,\ M$ and $D$.

parts.label: c
parts.latex: Given that $\dfrac{P}{Q}=\dfrac{5n+4}{9n+6}$, evaluate $\dfrac{10^{\text{th}}\text{ term of A}}{10^{\text{th}}\text{ term of B}}$.

solutions.latex:
For the first AP $\mathbf{A}$:

Sum of $n$ terms $P=\dfrac{n}{2}[2a+(n-1)d]$

and $n^{\text{th}}$ term $a_n=a+(n-1)d$

For the second AP $\mathbf{B}$:

Sum of $n$ terms $Q=\dfrac{n}{2}[2M+(n-1)D]$

and $n^{\text{th}}$ term $M_n=M+(n-1)D$

It is given that

$$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{\text{Sum of }n\text{ terms of first AP}}{\text{Sum of }n\text{ terms of second AP}}&=\dfrac{\frac{n}{2}[2a+(n-1)d]}{\frac{n}{2}[2M+(n-1)D]}\\&=\dfrac{[2a+(n-1)d]}{[2M+(n-1)D]}\\&=\dfrac{a+\left(\frac{n-1}{2}\right)d}{M+\left(\frac{n-1}{2}\right)D}\end{aligned}$$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: Correctly shows the sum of both AP's and simplifies to obtain the ratio needed

solutions.latex:
The ratio of the $10^{\text{th}}$ term of A and B:

$$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{10^{\text{th}}\text{ term of A}}{10^{\text{th}}\text{ term of B}}&=\dfrac{a_{10}\text{ of first AP}}{M_{10}\text{ of second AP}}\\&=\dfrac{a+(10-1)d}{M+(10-1)D}\\&=\dfrac{a+9d}{M+9D}\end{aligned}$$
